# ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry Weekly Report (Jun 21 - 27, 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
This week focused on stabilizing the Superchain ecosystem following the Karst hardfork, with a primary emphasis on gas management and registry hygiene. Key technical achievements included the introduction of configuration flags to address intrinsic gas issues on Sepolia and Mainnet, alongside the removal of deprecated testnet chains to streamline the registry. Development also progressed on foundational infrastructure, specifically regarding Rust stack release processes and the hardening of settlement and execution tests for the Superchain Dependency Manager (SDM).

## 🛠️ Key Developments

### Protocol Configuration & Hardfork Management
To address gas estimation anomalies following the Karst hardfork, the team introduced a new per-chain configuration flag, `keep_karst_upgrade_gas`. This flag was enabled for both Sepolia and Mainnet superchains to ensure consistent gas behavior and resolve "intrinsic gas too high" errors reported by users ([#1259](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/pull/1259)).

### Registry Maintenance and Automation
The registry underwent significant cleanup and routine maintenance to improve data integrity:
*   **Chain Deletion:** The Ethernity Testnet (ID 233) and Creator Chain Testnet (ID 66665) were removed from the registry, including their configuration TOMLs and genesis files ([#1263](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/pull/1263)).
*   **Automated Updates:** Routine CircleCI jobs performed automated codegen updates to `addresses.json` within the `superchain/extra` directory ([#1262](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/pull/1262)).

### Operational Tooling & Infrastructure
Improvements were made to the reliability of the registry's underlying tooling:
*   **Atomic File Operations:** The `AtomicWrite` function was refactored to stage temporary files within the destination directory, preventing `EXDEV` errors during cross-filesystem renames ([#1264](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/pull/1264)).
*   **SDM Hardening:** Significant work was completed to harden SDM tests, specifically covering ETH supply conservation and `PostExecSettlementUnderflow` execution paths ([#21324](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/21324)).

## 🐛 Issues & Triage

### Closed Issues
*   **Proving Cluster Service:** The request for a dedicated proof request/queue service for self-hosted clusters was closed. It was determined that `sp1-cluster` support is currently sufficient for SP-1 requirements ([#21462](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/21462)).
*   **Design Finalization:** The design document for PCD (Proof-Carry Data) Infrastructure support was officially approved and finalized ([#21327](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/21327)).

### New & Active Issues
*   **Reth Integration:** A new feature request was opened to integrate upstream slot-preimage seeding helpers into `op-reth` to improve snapshot importer efficiency ([#21523](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/21523)).
*   **Rust Stack Release Process:** Ongoing discussions highlight friction in the monorepo release process, specifically regarding outdated changelogs for `op-revm` (stuck at v19.0.0 despite v20.0.0 being live) and the need for better tracking of GitHub releases ([#18926](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/18926)).
*   **Kona-node Development:** Work continues on the `SafeDB` implementation for `kona-node`. Developers are currently experimenting with a `SafeDBv1` trait for parity with existing systems while designing a more robust `SafeDBv2` for interoperability and proofs ([#20278](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/20278)).
*   **Interop Recovery:** The development of a runbook for recovering chains after invalid interop messages has been delayed by one week due to competing project priorities ([#21161](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/21161)).

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
Collaboration this week was characterized by high-level design discussions regarding the Rust-based stack and interoperability. Technical leads (including `geoknee`, `einar-oplabs`, and `yuercl`) were active in diagnosing the Karst hardfork gas issues and refining the `SafeDB` architecture. The interaction between community bug reports (regarding gas limits) and rapid configuration fixes demonstrates a tight feedback loop between users and maintainers.
